title: "... swallows typos"

reponse: '4'
attendu: "`3`, or an error about the misspelled argument"

::: {.piege}
```{r}
sum(1, 2, na.rm = TRUE)
sum(1, 2, na.rn = TRUE)
paste(c("a", "b"), colapse = "+")
```
:::

## Why

`sum()` and `paste()` accept any number of values through `...`. An argument whose name is not recognised is not rejected: it joins the data. `na.rn = TRUE` becomes the value `TRUE`, that is 1, added to the sum. `colapse = "+"` becomes one more string to paste.

## The remedy

Double-check argument names, and in your own functions, reject anything unexpected in `...`, for instance with `rlang::check_dots_empty()`.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
sum(c(1, 2, NA), na.rm = TRUE)
paste(c("a", "b"), collapse = "+")
```
:::
